acceptable-soreness: Muscles that have worked will ache. As a rule of thumb, discomfort up to about 4 or 5 out of 10 during and after exercise is acceptable, provided it settles back to your normal level within 24 hours and is not getting worse week on week. Sharp, sudden or one-sided pain is a reason to stop.
little-and-often: Short daily sessions beat one long weekly effort. The programmes below are designed to be done in ten to twenty minutes, most days, in your own kitchen or hallway.
consistency: Almost every trial that produced a real result ran for at least eight to twelve weeks. Judge the programme at three months, not at three days.
stress-page: My separate page on [stress management]({{links.stress}}) takes you through the same relaxation techniques in more detail, including the breathing and progressive muscle relaxation practices referred to here.
not-medical-advice: This sheet is general information for my patients. If you have been given different, specific advice about your own condition, that advice comes first.
corridor-rule: Do this in a corridor narrow enough that you can touch both walls with your elbows out, or beside a kitchen bench. Never in the middle of a room.
